# Text markup: what any text in Mathium can hold

<!-- Generated by `npm run catalog` from the text tools' entries (packages/present/src/markup/). Edit those, not this. -->

One page for whoever writes text for a page (a person, the course generator, the margin tutor). Every piece below
works in any prose: a lesson's `p` block, a caption, a tutor's answer. Each is checked and has a plain fallback, so a
mistake shows as plain text, never as a broken page. Design: `docs/design/ENGINE-ZONES.md` (the text zone),
`docs/design/ENGINE-ARCH.md` (how a tool is added), `docs/design/specimen` (the experiments they come from).

| You want | Write | The learner sees | For |
|---|---|---|---|
| a word in the colour of its thing in the figure | `[cost](noun:cost)` | the word in the noun's colour; touching it lights its thing in the figures on the page, and touching the thing lights the word | course authors |
| a definition that opens in its sentence | `[convex](def: a set that holds every segment between two of its points)` | a dotted term; tapped, the definition opens right after it on a faint ground and the rest of the sentence steps down (a definition may hold definitions) | everyone, the tutor too |
| a number in a sentence the learner drags | `{{n = 3, 1..12}}` or `{{rate = 0.5, 0..2, 0.1}}` (value, range, step) | a glass number; drag it sideways (or arrow keys); a figure bound to it follows | everyone, the tutor too |
| a number computed from the ones the learner drags | `{{= 2.5*n}}` or `{{= 2.5*n, 2}}` (2 decimals) | it follows as you drag, every digit a wheel | everyone, the tutor too |
| a claim with its chain of reasons, each opened on demand | a ```` ```why ```` fence (below) | the claim with a hollow ring; tapped, its reasons drop on threads, down to a definition or an assumption | everyone, the tutor too |
| a derivation written line by line, every line checked | a ```` ```steps ```` fence (below) | written line by line, each line coming down out of the one above, every line checked | everyone, the tutor too |
| a formula that comes apart, each part with what it means | a ```` ```parts ```` fence (below) | the formula; tapped, each part lifts on a card with its meaning | everyone, the tutor too |
| more, folded under the sentence, for who wants it | a ```` ```details ```` fence (below) | a title; tapped, the rest unfolds like folded paper | course authors |
| a source, condensed as glass beside its mark | `[^key]` (and a `cite` block with that key) | a small number; tapped, the source condenses as glass beside it | course authors |

Also: `$inline TeX$`, `$$display TeX$$`, `**bold**` (the one key idea), `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `[text](https://…)`.

```why
A function differentiable at $x_0$ is continuous there.
- the difference is the quotient times $h$, and that tends to 0
  - the quotient tends to $f'(x_0)$
    - that is what differentiable means [definition]
  - a limit of a product is the product of the limits [assumption]
- so there is no jump at $x_0$
```

The first line is the claim; each `- ` line is a reason; two spaces deeper is a reason for the reason. End a chain at bedrock with `[definition]` or `[assumption]` (`[定义]` / `[假设]`); at most three deep. Only for a claim a reader would doubt.

```steps
% nouns: x_0 = value
2x + 3 = 11
2x = 8        % subtract 3 from both sides
x = 4         % divide both sides by 2
```

One complete TeX formula per line, 2 to 8 lines, one change per line; `%` and a few words for what was done. The optional first line `% nouns: x_0 = value, f = function` draws those symbols in their noun's colour.

```parts
P(A\mid B) = \frac{P(B\mid A)\,P(A)}{P(B)}
P(A\mid B): how likely A is, now that B is seen
P(B\mid A): how likely B is if A is true
P(A): how common A is before any evidence
P(B): how common the evidence is
```

The formula on the first line; then each part as it is written in the formula, a colon, and what it means. For a formula whose parts are the lesson.

```details Why the gradient is held by the active constraint
At the optimum the cost cannot fall along the wall.

$\nabla J + \lambda \nabla g = 0,\ \lambda \ge 0$
```

The title on the fence line; each paragraph of the body is one sheet of the fold.

- **noun**: only the nouns the page's figures draw (their roles), so the colour means the same thing in both.
- **def**: only for a term this reader may not know; the first time the term appears, instead of a sentence of definition that interrupts the argument.
- **number**: only where "what if it were bigger?" is the point of the paragraph; the numbers of one page share their names (a figure can bind to them).
- **computed**: names are words (cups, rate, n); + − * / ^ ( ), sqrt, abs, round, min, max, log, exp, sin, cos.

## In lesson data

The same pieces as blocks (`packages/core/src/content.ts`): `{ "type": "why", "claim", "because": [{ "text", "kind"?,
"because"? }] }`; `{ "type": "steps", "lines": [{ "tex", "why"? }], "nouns"? }`; `{ "type": "math", "tex", "parts": [{
"tex", "says" }] }`; `{ "type": "details", "summary", "blocks" }`; `{ "type": "visual", …, "bind": { "<figure param>":
"<number's name>" } }` (the figure follows a number of the page's text, and moves it back). Inline pieces (nouns,
definitions, numbers) go in any text string.

## Rules of use

- One of each where it helps; a page is not a showcase. A definition only for a term this reader may not know; a
  chain of why only for a claim a reader would doubt; numbers to drag only where "what if it were bigger?" is the
  point.
- Nouns: only the nouns the page's figures draw (their roles), so the colour means the same thing in both.
- Never instructions in the text ("tap the ring", "drag the number"): the page shows what can be done.

## Adding a tool

A new tool is one file in `packages/present/src/markup/` with its `define_markup` entry: how it is written, what the
learner sees, the words the tutor and the course generator are told, a `check` for a malformed use, and its renderer
(`html`; `pattern` for an inline one). It starts as `maturity: 'experiment'` (the gallery only), and this guide, the
tutor's prompt and the course format pick it up when it is promoted (`npm run catalog`).
